questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $(x-1)$ and $(x+1)$ are factors of the polynomial $f(x) = ax^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 + bx - 3$, find the values of the constants $a$ and $b$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
If $(x-1)$ is a factor, then $f(1) = 0$ (factor theorem). If $(x+1)$ is a factor, then $f(-1) = 0$.

$$
f(1) = a + 7 + 1 + b - 3 = a + b + 5 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a + b = -5. \tag{1}
$$

$$
f(-1) = a - 7 + 1 - b - 3 = a - b - 9 = 0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a - b = 9. \tag{2}
$$

Adding (1) and (2): $2a = 4$, so $a = 2$. Then from (1): $b = -5 - 2 = -7$.

Check: $f(x) = 2x^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 - 7x - 3$, so $f(1) = 2 + 7 + 1 - 7 - 3 = 0$ and $f(-1) = 2 - 7 + 1 + 7 - 3 = 0$.

$$\boxed{a = 2,\quad b = -7}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = ax^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 + bx - 3$ with $(x-1)$ and $(x+1)$ as factors, hence find the set of real values of $x$ for which $f(x) > 0$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the previous part, $f(x) = 2x^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 - 7x - 3$. Since $(x-1)(x+1) = x^2 - 1$ is a factor, divide by $x^2 - 1$:

$$2x^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 - 7x - 3 = (x^2 - 1)(2x^2 + 7x + 3).$$

Check by expanding: $(x^2-1)(2x^2+7x+3) = 2x^4 + 7x^3 + 3x^2 - 2x^2 - 7x - 3 = 2x^4 + 7x^3 + x^2 - 7x - 3$. Correct.

Factorise the quadratic: $2x^2 + 7x + 3 = (2x+1)(x+3)$. Hence

$$f(x) = (x-1)(x+1)(2x+1)(x+3).$$

The four roots, in increasing order, are $x = -3,\ -1,\ -\tfrac12,\ 1$. The leading coefficient $2$ is positive and every root is simple, so the sign of $f$ alternates, starting with $+$ on the far right:

| interval | $x<-3$ | $-3<x<-1$ | $-1<x<-\tfrac12$ | $-\tfrac12<x<1$ | $x>1$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sign of $f(x)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ | $+$ |

Check with test values: $f(-4) = (-5)(-3)(-7)(-1) = 105 > 0$; $f(-2) = (-3)(-1)(-3)(1) = -9 < 0$; $f(-0.75) = (-1.75)(0.25)(-0.5)(2.25) \approx 0.49 > 0$; $f(0) = -3 < 0$; $f(2) = (1)(3)(5)(5) = 75 > 0$.

$$\boxed{\{x \in \mathbb{R} : x < -3\} \cup \{x : -1 < x < -\tfrac12\} \cup \{x : x > 1\}}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $m \log_3 2 = 10 \log_9 6$. Find the values of $m$. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Change both logarithms to the same base $3$, using $\log_9 6 = \dfrac{\log_3 6}{\log_3 9} = \dfrac{\log_3 6}{2}$:

$$m \log_3 2 = 10\cdot\frac{\log_3 6}{2} = 5\log_3 6 = 5(\log_3 2 + \log_3 3) = 5(\log_3 2 + 1).$$

Hence

$$m = \frac{5(\log_3 2 + 1)}{\log_3 2} = \frac{5\log_3 6}{\log_3 2}.$$

By the change of base formula $\dfrac{\log_3 6}{\log_3 2} = \log_2 6$, so

$$\boxed{m = 5\log_2 6 = 5 + 5\log_2 3 \approx 12.92}$$

Numerical check: $\log_2 3 = 1.58496$, so $m = 5 + 7.9248 = 12.9248$. Then $m\log_3 2 = 12.9248 \times 0.63093 = 8.1546$ and $10\log_9 6 = 10 \times 0.81546 = 8.1546$. Both sides agree.

There is only one value of $m$ (the equation is linear in $m$).
